nodes.description:
There is no treatment that restores ciliary function. Management is the supportive care used across primary ciliary dyskinesia: airway clearance, prompt treatment of respiratory infections, and macrolide prophylaxis, for which a randomized trial of azithromycin in PCD reduced pulmonary exacerbations. Nothing in it is specific to DNAH11. The cilia still move, but clearance fails, so the same airway care applies as in immotile-cilia PCD.
Curated as a single scoping entry rather than an itemised regimen, because no trial has enrolled by genotype and the umbrella Primary_Ciliary_Dyskinesia entry holds the detailed management block.

evidence.snippet: Though there are no PCD-specific approved therapies that restore ciliary function, routine airway clearance and aggressive management of infections are important to preserve lung health and minimize complications

evidence.snippet: A European study found that people with PCD benefitted from treatment with thrice weekly azithromycin, with decreased pulmonary exacerbation rates and without an apparent increase in antibiotic resistance

nodes.description: Most DNAH11 alleles are nonsense, frameshift or splice variants; all are private. DNAH11 protein is lost from the cilium in patients with loss-of-function alleles.
